title: The World Wide Web is invented at CERN

when.label: March 1989 – August 1991
when.note: From Tim Berners-Lee's first proposal (March 1989) to his public announcement of the WWW software (August 1991).

summary: Working at the CERN physics laboratory, Tim Berners-Lee proposed and built the World Wide Web, running the first website on a NeXT computer in his office.
description: Tim Berners-Lee wrote the first proposal for the World Wide Web in March 1989; with Robert Cailliau it was formalised as a management proposal in November 1990. By the end of 1990 he had the first web server and browser running at CERN on a NeXT computer labelled 'This machine is a server. DO NOT POWER IT DOWN!!'

info.cern.ch was the world's first website. In 1991 Berners-Lee released his WWW software, including a simple line-mode browser written by Nicola Pellow; it became available to colleagues at CERN in March 1991 and was announced on internet newsgroups in August 1991.
context: Early in 1993 the National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA) at the University of Illinois released the first version of its Mosaic browser.

facts.text: Berners-Lee wrote the first proposal in March 1989.
The first web server and browser were running at CERN by the end of 1990.
info.cern.ch was the address of the world's first website and web server.
